**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
- Multiple corn stalks lying flat, showing advanced decomposition
- Central stalk has distinctive yellow-green discoloration with dark black patches/lesions on the outer surface
- Stalks appear bleached/pale gray externally with fibrous breakdown
- Black fungal material visible on surfaces

**Key Observations vs. Reference:**
The Anthracnose stalk rot reference (bottom-left panel) shows exactly this pattern: dark black external lesions on stalks with yellow-green transitional coloration, matching the test image's central stalk. The fibrous stalk degradation and external black discoloration on the outer rind are hallmarks of *Colletotrichum graminicola* (anthracnose stalk rot). The bleached outer surface combined with black lesions is characteristic.

This is not Physoderma stalk rot (which shows distinct banding at nodes), not Diplodia (white mycelium inside), and not Charcoal rot (gray-black pith with microsclerotia).
